changes.before: Complete readMode(env). Missing APP_MODE defaults to "development". Exactly "development" and "production" are accepted; all other values return null. Do not change env or log its contents.
changes.after: Use a default only when a setting is missing. Reject values the app does not understand.

before: Environment variables are configuration values supplied outside your source code.
In Node.js, process.env reads the process environment. Values such as "false" arrive as text, not Boolean false.
process.env belongs to Node, not the browser. The browser practice receives an ordinary object instead, so the reading logic can be tested safely.
A default answers what to do when a value is missing. It should not silently replace a present but invalid value.
This accepts small and large. A present empty string is invalid, not the default.
Configuration can contain secrets. Do not print the entire environment, paste secrets into lessons, or commit a real secret file to Git.
For this practice, APP_MODE is not a secret. Still, return only the selected mode rather than exposing unrelated settings.
Use a missing value, both accepted values, and an unknown value to test the decision. Preserve the input object.
after: An environment variable is a setting supplied when a program starts. It lets you change a setting without editing the source code.
Node reads these settings through process.env. Their values are text: "false" is text, not the boolean false.
A default is the value used when a setting was not supplied. Choose it deliberately.
The browser has no Node process.env. Our practice receives an ordinary object instead, so the decision can be tested.
Only undefined counts as missing in this exercise. A present but unrecognized value must return null.
An empty string is still a supplied value. It is not one of the allowed sizes, so it is rejected.
An environment may contain secrets. Do not print or copy the whole environment just to inspect one setting.
For the exercise, read only APP_MODE. Return the mode and leave the input object unchanged.
Complete readMode(env). Missing APP_MODE becomes "development". Accept exactly "development" or "production". Return null for every other value.

before: Make one change to the starter.
Explain why a changed input produces its result.
after: Use development only when APP_MODE is undefined.
Check the result against the two allowed names.
Return null for an invalid value.
Run the checks without changing or logging env.

before: Distinguish undefined from a present empty string.
Compare exactly with the two accepted names.
Do not mutate or print the input object.
after: Compare with undefined rather than testing whether the value is truthy.
Use exact comparisons with the two allowed names.

before.question: APP_MODE is an empty string, not missing. Under this contract, should readMode use development?
choices: Yes; empty and missing always mean the same thing.
No; the present empty value is invalid and should return null.
before.explanation: The default is only for an omitted setting. Treating every falsy value as missing would conceal invalid configuration.

after.question: APP_MODE is an empty string. Should this rule use development?
choices: Yes. Empty and missing always mean the same thing.
No. The present empty value is invalid, so return null.
after.explanation: Only a missing setting gets the default. Empty text is present but not accepted.

changes.before: Only the reading logic runs in the browser. In a local Node project, call readMode(process.env). Environment values are supplied by the operating system or launcher; this lesson does not configure your device.
changes.after: The browser uses a supplied object. A local Node program can call readMode(process.env). This lesson does not change your computer's environment settings.

project.title: Read a setting without hard-coding it
project.task: Complete readMode(env). Default missing APP_MODE to development. Accept exactly development or production; return null otherwise. Do not change or log env.
project.done_when: Checks pass for missing, valid, empty, and unknown values. Explain why empty text is not the same as a missing setting.
